data.narrative: Student completed Module 1 containerization: chose Debian Slim base image for psycopg2 compatibility, designed multi-stage Dockerfile with layer cache optimization, implemented security hardening (non-root user, HEALTHCHECK). Diagnosed and fixed BREAK bug: identified cache-busting caused by COPY order (moved requirements before app code). Demonstrated understanding of reproducibility problem containers solve.

dimension_scores.observation: Student created production-appropriate Dockerfile with multi-stage build, layer caching strategy, and security hardening.
dimension_scores.evidence: Dockerfile uses FROM...AS builder pattern, copies requirements before RUN pip install (cache optimization), non-root USER appuser, HEALTHCHECK with /live endpoint, .dockerignore to exclude .git/__pycache__/.env.

dimension_scores.observation: Student understands containerization as first step of pipeline; pipeline design (CI/CD automation) deferred to Module 2.
dimension_scores.evidence: Student stated: 'we build this image manually on our laptop. There is no automated pipeline to build, test, and deploy it. That is Module 02.' Shows awareness of deployment pipeline scope.

dimension_scores.observation: Student implemented HEALTHCHECK endpoint; deeper observability (logging, metrics, alerts) not yet in scope.
dimension_scores.evidence: Dockerfile includes: HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --retries=3 CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/live. Health probe is observability foundation.

dimension_scores.observation: Student anticipated build-time failure (BREAK bug on cache invalidation) and source-level failure (missing environment consistency); runtime failures not yet explored.
dimension_scores.evidence: Debugged COPY order bug: 'COPY . . after pip install invalidates cache on source changes—expensive rebuild.' Explained Python 3.8 vs 3.11 reproducibility risk.

dimension_scores.observation: Degradation design not yet covered in Module 1; student understands graceful degradation concept but not yet implemented circuit breakers or fallback logic.
dimension_scores.evidence: Student defined graceful degradation accurately in PRETEST but no degradation implemented in Dockerfile. Scope for Modules 5-6.

dimension_scores.observation: Dockerfile includes inline comments explaining layer purpose and security decisions; runbook documentation deferred to Module 7.
dimension_scores.evidence: Comments: '# Copy requirements FIRST (changes to requirements.txt invalidate cache)', '# Copy only necessary files from builder (venv + app code)', '# Create a non-root user for security'.

strengths: Strong decision-making: chose Debian Slim over Alpine with clear reasoning (psycopg2 glibc compatibility > image size trade-off for single daily deploy).
Rapid debugging: identified BREAK bug independently—understood layer cache principle well enough to see COPY order was wrong.
Security awareness: implemented all hardening controls (non-root user, .dockerignore, HEALTHCHECK) without prompting.
growth_areas: Degradation design not yet practiced; will deepen in Modules 5-6 when introducing circuit breakers and fallback patterns.
Pipeline design scope limited to single image build; CI/CD automation and deployment safety covered in Module 2.
data.recommendation: In Module 2, extend this containerized service into a CI/CD pipeline: automate image builds on git push, run tests before image creation, and implement deployment gates (staging before production). This connects 'container works locally' to 'container deploys safely everywhere.'

public_evidence.student_action: Designed and implemented multi-stage Dockerfile with layer cache optimization and security hardening for URL shortener service.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Multi-stage build: Stage 1 (builder) copies requirements first, runs pip install, then copies app code; Stage 2 (runtime) copies only venv + app from builder, runs as non-root user appuser. HEALTHCHECK probes /live endpoint.
public_evidence.proof: api/Dockerfile (39 lines): FROM python:3.12-slim AS builder, COPY requirements.txt, RUN pip install, COPY app/alembic/scripts, FROM python:3.12-slim, COPY --from=builder, RUN groupadd -r appgroup && useradd -r, USER appuser, HEALTHCHECK.
public_evidence.ability: Designs containerized applications with layer caching strategy, security hardening, and health observability.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows mastery of Dockerfile optimization (copy order, multi-stage), security (non-root user, .dockerignore), and operational readiness (HEALTHCHECK). Demonstrates production thinking: reproducibility, attack surface minimization, deployment safety.

public_evidence.student_action: Created .dockerignore to exclude unnecessary/sensitive files from build context, reducing image size and preventing secret leaks.
public_evidence.ability: Understands build context impact on image size, deployment speed, and security; implements file exclusion discipline.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows attention to operational details that prevent bloated images and accidental secret exposure in production artifacts.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Correctly explained: COPY requirements.txt first, RUN pip install (cached if requirements unchanged), THEN COPY app code (source changes don't invalidate install layer). Identified and fixed BREAK bug using this principle.

Implemented builder stage (compiles/installs) and runtime stage (runs only); explained: 'builder has compilers and dev tools, runtime has only venv + app—runtime image is 80%+ smaller with no build bloat.'
Implemented non-root user: 'groupadd -r appgroup && useradd -r -g appgroup -s /bin/false appuser'; reasoning: 'even if container breached, attacker lands as limited user not root.'
Explained Python 3.8 vs 3.11 problem: 'Direct scp deployment means teammate needs exact OS/Python version; containers ship identical runtime everywhere, preventing surprises.'

teaching_approaches.detail: BREAK bug made caching tangible: reordering COPY operations from 'copy all then install' to 'copy requirements, install, copy code' directly showed impact on rebuild speed.
Python 3.8 vs 3.11 incident from CONTEXT step resonated as concrete example of why 'works locally' fails without containerization.

learning_style_signals: Learns well from concrete failures (BREAK bug made layer caching vivid)
Connects to prior experience (Module 3 race conditions parallel to cache invalidation timing issues)
Benefits from specific reasoning (chose Debian Slim with rationale, not just default)
